_metadata.description: Draft C1-C12 annotations for 8 top Tier-A expansion candidates
_metadata.status: APPROVED 2026-04-23 — graph_ids ata_thyroid_storm_2016 -> jta_jes_thyroid_storm_2016, aasld_acute_liver_failure_2023 -> acg_acute_liver_failure_2023 corrected; 4 conservative values confirmed (ADA HHS C2=0, UKKA C5=0, ACOG C9=0, WMS C2=1).

ada_hhs_2024.guideline_name: Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes: A Consensus Report (ADA/EASD/JBDS-IP/AACE/DTS)
ada_hhs_2024.c2_evidence_system: Consensus report (no formal grading; PRISMA-guided literature search)
ada_hhs_2024._c2_note: Source text: 'The guidance represents the panel's collective analysis, evaluation, and expert opinion' — no GRADE/ADA-A-B-C-E applied; older ADA position statement had A/B/C/E but this 2024 consensus report did not use it.
ada_hhs_2024.c7_source_text: HHS develops over days-to-weeks but decompensated HHS with profound hyperosmolarity carries mortality 5-20%; glucose decline rate must not exceed 90-120 mg/dL/h to prevent cerebral edema.
ada_hhs_2024.c8_source_text: 'The rate of decline of serum sodium should not exceed 10 mmol/L in 24 h'; 'The rate of fall in osmolality should be no greater than 3.0-8.0 mOsm/kg/h'; 'glucose reduction should not exceed 90 to 120 mg/dL per hour'; 'Routine bicarbonate administration is not recommended'; 'administration of 0.45% sodium chloride is indicated only if osmolality is not declining despite adequate positive fluid balance'; insulin delayed until K >3.5 mmol/L.
ada_hhs_2024._c9_note: Figure 4 'Treatment pathways for DKA and HHS' (combined algorithm) + Figure 2B 'Diagnosis criteria of HHS'; only one true treatment algorithm covers HHS explicitly.
ada_hhs_2024.c10_source_text: 'Initial rate of 500-1,000 mL/h during the first 2-4 h'; 'Measuring serum potassium 2 h after starting insulin administration and every 4 h thereafter'; glucose decline <=90-120 mg/dL/h; Na decline <=10 mmol/L/24h; osmolality fall 3-8 mOsm/kg/h.
ada_hhs_2024.c11_source_text: 'If low-normal or low potassium levels (<3.5 mmol/L) are present on admission... potassium replacement should begin... and insulin therapy should be delayed until the potassium level increases to >3.5 mmol/L' — K replacement BEFORE insulin in hypokalemic patients.
ada_hhs_2024.c12_source_text: 'If HHS is present with no ketosis or with mild or moderate ketonemia... fixed-rate intravenous insulin infusion should be started at 0.05 units/kg/h. If significant ketonemia is present (i.e., beta-hydroxybutyrate >=3.0 mmol/L... pH <7.30... or bicarbonate <18 mmol/L), which represents mixed DKA/HHS... 0.1 units/kg/h.' DKA vs HHS vs mixed branching.

jta_jes_thyroid_storm_2016.guideline_name: 2016 Guidelines for the Management of Thyroid Storm from the Japan Thyroid Association and Japan Endocrine Society (First Edition)
jta_jes_thyroid_storm_2016.publisher: Japan Thyroid Association (JTA) / Japan Endocrine Society (JES)
jta_jes_thyroid_storm_2016._publisher_note: Candidate ID is 'ata_thyroid_storm_2016' but the 2016 guideline is actually from JTA/JES (not ATA). The ATA 2016 guideline is on hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis, not thyroid storm specifically. Reviewer should confirm naming.
jta_jes_thyroid_storm_2016.c2_evidence_system: ACP Guideline Grading System (strength of recommendation: strong/weak; quality of evidence: high/moderate/low/insufficient)
jta_jes_thyroid_storm_2016._c2_note: Source text: 'In these recommendations, which use the Guideline Grading System developed by the American College of Physicians (ACP), both strength of recommendation and quality of evidence were evaluated based on the criteria shown in Table 1.' ACP system is a society-adapted GRADE-like system scored as 1 under v2 rubric.
jta_jes_thyroid_storm_2016.c6_gbd_cause: Endocrine, metabolic, blood, and immune disorders (other)
jta_jes_thyroid_storm_2016._c6_note: Thyroid storm is rare (~0.2/100k) but has ~11% mortality per the guideline nationwide survey; not in GBD Top-15 but a recognized endocrine emergency.
jta_jes_thyroid_storm_2016.c7_source_text: 'detailed analyses of clinical data from 356 patients revealed that the mortality was still high (~11%) with multiple organ failure and acute heart failure being common causes of death' — minutes-to-hours for cardiogenic shock/CNS deterioration.
jta_jes_thyroid_storm_2016.c8_source_text: 'Non-steroid anti-inflammatory agents as well as aspirin are not recommended because these drugs may increase free thyroid hormone levels [46]'; 'Although the non-selective beta-AA propranolol is not contraindicated, it is not recommended for the treatment of tachycardia in thyroid storm' in Killip class >=IV; iodide contraindicated in patients with painless thyroiditis; high-dose corticosteroid cautions.
jta_jes_thyroid_storm_2016._c9_note: Figures 1-9 are referenced in the paper; Fig 2 'Medical treatment for convulsions (algorithm)', Fig 3 'Differential diagnosis of CNS manifestations (algorithm)', Fig 4 'Algorithm for diagnostic considerations in thyroid storm', Figs 6-8 on antithyroid drug/iodide/corticosteroid use, Fig 5 ICU triage. >=5 algorithm figures justify score 2.
jta_jes_thyroid_storm_2016.c10_source_text: Acetaminophen 500 mg three times per day; beta-blocker selection depends on HR thresholds (HR >=150 bpm: landiolol/esmolol IV; HR <150: oral beta1-selective); iodide started concurrently with ATDs; ICU admission criteria tied to Killip class.
jta_jes_thyroid_storm_2016.c11_source_text: 'either methimazole (MMI) or propylthiouracil (PTU) can be the first-line option, and inorganic iodide should be administered concurrently with ATDs to patients with TS caused by thyrotoxic diseases associated with hyperthyroidism' — ATDs BEFORE or WITH iodide (never iodide alone).
jta_jes_thyroid_storm_2016.c12_source_text: 15 recommendations branch across CNS (convulsions algorithm), cardiovascular (Killip class <=III vs IV), hepato-GI organ failure; treatment branches on HR threshold 150 bpm; ICU admission criteria by clinical severity.

ukka_hyperkalemia_2023.guideline_name: UKKA Clinical Practice Guideline: Treatment of Acute Hyperkalaemia in Adults (2023 Update)
ukka_hyperkalemia_2023._c2_note: Source text: 'The recommendations in each guideline statement have been graded using the GRADE system'; strength 1/2, quality A/B/C/D.
ukka_hyperkalemia_2023._c5_note: No DOI discoverable; published as UKKA website PDF (ukkidney.org). Persistent URL: https://www.ukkidney.org/sites/renal.org/files/FINAL%20VERSION%20-%20UKKA%20CLINICAL%20PRACTICE%20GUIDELINE%20-%20MANAGEMENT%20OF%20HYPERKALAEMIA%20IN%20ADULTS%20-%20191223.pdf . Society-hosted persistent URL may satisfy C5=1 per rubric, but conservative score applied.
ukka_hyperkalemia_2023.c7_source_text: 'may precede cardiac arrest - wide QRS complex, bradycardia or sine wave (Guidelines 14.1-14.2; Figure 3)'; severe hyperkalaemia with ECG changes = minutes-to-hours to arrest.
ukka_hyperkalemia_2023.c8_source_text: 'Calcium resonium should no longer be routinely used in the management of acute hyperkalaemia'; 'Sodium bicarbonate not used routinely for the acute treatment of hyperkalaemia'; 'SPS and CPS are no longer recommended in the acute'; 'MRAs should be avoided in patients with a baseline serum K+ >5.0 mmol/l'; 'Macrogol 3350 should be avoided as it contains potassium'; 'Diuretics should be avoided in patients who are hypovolaemic'.
ukka_hyperkalemia_2023._c9_note: Figure 1 (ECG progression), Figure 2 (ECG example), Figure 3 (arrhythmias), Figure 4 (5-step treatment algorithm); plus Appendix 6/7/8 algorithms (Community, Hospital, Cardiac Arrest).
ukka_hyperkalemia_2023.c10_source_text: '30ml 10% Calcium Gluconate over 10 minutes OR 10ml 10% Calcium Chloride over 5 minutes'; blood glucose monitoring at 0/30/60/90/120/180/240/300/360 min post-insulin; 12-lead ECG urgent if K+ >=6.0; K+ repeat within 1 day for K+ 6.0-6.4 and within 3 days for 5.5-5.9; insulin-glucose over 15 min.
ukka_hyperkalemia_2023.c11_source_text: 'logical 5-step approach: 1. Protect the heart (IV calcium salts first); 2. Shift K+ into cells (insulin-glucose, salbutamol); 3. Remove K+ from body; 4. Monitor blood; 5. Assess need for dialysis' — calcium BEFORE insulin-glucose shift is mandatory sequence.
ukka_hyperkalemia_2023.c12_source_text: K+ severity tiers: mild 5.5-5.9, moderate 6.0-6.4, severe >=6.5 each with distinct actions; pre-treatment blood glucose <7.0 triggers dextrose infusion branch; community vs hospital vs cardiac arrest algorithms; RAASi cessation at K+ >=6.0.

sccm_delirium_padis_2018.guideline_name: Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Prevention and Management of Pain, Agitation/Sedation, Delirium, Immobility, and Sleep Disruption in Adult Patients in the ICU
sccm_delirium_padis_2018._c2_note: [ABSTRACT] 'sections searched the best available evidence, determined its quality, and formulated recommendations as strong, conditional, or good practice statements based on Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation principles.'
sccm_delirium_padis_2018._c5_note: Full manuscript DOI 10.1097/CCM.0000000000003299 (pp e825-e873); executive summary at 10.1097/CCM.0000000000003259. Either can be cited.
sccm_delirium_padis_2018.c6_gbd_cause: ICU-acquired complications (no single GBD cause; PADIS addresses delirium, a top contributor to ICU mortality)
sccm_delirium_padis_2018._c6_note: Delirium not in GBD Top-15 but is a major ICU outcome driver; PADIS targets are cross-cutting.
sccm_delirium_padis_2018.c7_source_text: [ABSTRACT] Pain/sedation/delirium harms accumulate over hours-to-days (ICU LOS, ventilator days, post-ICU cognitive impairment). Not minutes-to-hours time-critical like sepsis/STEMI.
sccm_delirium_padis_2018.c8_source_text: [ABSTRACT + society summary] 'We recommend propofol or dexmedetomidine over benzodiazepines' (benzodiazepines implicitly discouraged for delirium); 'We suggest against using haloperidol or an atypical antipsychotic to prevent delirium'; 'We suggest using light sedation (vs deep sedation)' (deep sedation discouraged); avoid routine use of rivastigmine; avoid routine pharmacologic sleep aids.
sccm_delirium_padis_2018._c9_note: [ABSTRACT-based] Landing page and executive summary do not describe discrete algorithm/flowchart figures; the PADIS guideline is organized as recommendation tables rather than flowcharts. Conservative score 0; reviewer should confirm against full PDF.
sccm_delirium_padis_2018.c10_source_text: 'sedation to be assessed in ICU patients at least every four hours using validated tools'; daily spontaneous awakening trial (SAT) and sedation interruption (implicit daily frequency).
sccm_delirium_padis_2018.c11_source_text: 'assessment of pain should precede sedation titration' — treat pain BEFORE increasing sedation (analgesia-first principle); RASS before CAM-ICU assessment (patient must be arousable to screen for delirium).
sccm_delirium_padis_2018.c12_source_text: CAM-ICU positive vs negative → distinct intervention arms; mechanically ventilated vs non-ventilated patients different sedation recommendations; light vs deep sedation branching by indication.

acg_acute_liver_failure_2023.guideline_name: ACG Clinical Guideline: Acute Liver Failure
acg_acute_liver_failure_2023._publisher_note: Candidate ID says 'aasld_acute_liver_failure_2023' but the 2023 ALF guideline is published by ACG (Shingina et al, Am J Gastroenterol 2023;118:1128-1153), not AASLD. AASLD has a 2023 guidance on acute-on-chronic liver failure (Karvellas et al, Hepatology). Reviewer should disambiguate.
acg_acute_liver_failure_2023._c2_note: [ABSTRACT] 'The scientific evidence was reviewed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation process to develop recommendations.'
acg_acute_liver_failure_2023.c6_gbd_cause: Cirrhosis and other chronic liver diseases (broader) / Acute hepatic failure (specific)
acg_acute_liver_failure_2023._c6_note: Acute liver failure is rare (~2000 cases/yr in US) but cirrhosis/chronic liver disease is GBD Top-20; ALF carries ~30% mortality without transplant.
acg_acute_liver_failure_2023.c7_source_text: [ABSTRACT] 'Acute liver failure (ALF) is defined as a rare, acute, potentially reversible condition resulting in severe liver impairment and rapid clinical deterioration' — hours-to-days window for transplant listing and NAC in APAP toxicity.
acg_acute_liver_failure_2023.c8_source_text: [ABSTRACT + summary] Cautions against sedation masking encephalopathy grade III/IV; 'In patients with acetaminophen toxicity, early administration of N-acetylcysteine is recommended' (implicitly contraindicated to delay); against prophylactic antibiotics without infection evidence; against steroids for non-autoimmune etiology; against hypertonic saline outside ICP management.
acg_acute_liver_failure_2023._c9_note: [ABSTRACT-based] Guideline Central summary indicates at least one diagnostic/etiology algorithm figure; conservative count of 1. Reviewer should confirm against full PDF.
acg_acute_liver_failure_2023.c10_source_text: [SUMMARY] NAC administration timing (ideally within 8-10 hours for APAP ingestion but recommended even at delayed presentation); transplant evaluation within 24h of ALF diagnosis; ICP monitoring for grade III/IV encephalopathy.
acg_acute_liver_failure_2023.c11_source_text: [SUMMARY] Identify etiology BEFORE specific therapy (viral serologies, autoimmune markers, APAP level); stabilize airway BEFORE transfer for grade III/IV encephalopathy; KCC/MELD calculation BEFORE transplant listing.
acg_acute_liver_failure_2023.c12_source_text: [ABSTRACT + summary] APAP vs non-APAP etiology branches (NAC recommended vs suggested); King's College Criteria OR MELD >25 defines high-risk branch for transplant listing; encephalopathy grade I-IV determines ICU admission/airway protection.

acog_preeclampsia_pb222_2020.guideline_name: Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia: ACOG Practice Bulletin, Number 222
acog_preeclampsia_pb222_2020.publisher: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)
acog_preeclampsia_pb222_2020._c2_note: Source text: 'Level A—Recommendations are based on good and consistent scientific evidence'; 'Level B—Recommendations are based on limited or inconsistent scientific evidence'; 'Level C—Recommendations are based primarily on consensus and expert opinion.' Society-specific grading → score 1.
acog_preeclampsia_pb222_2020._c6_note: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy are a leading cause of maternal mortality per Lancet Commission; preeclampsia complicates 2-8% of pregnancies globally per the bulletin.
acog_preeclampsia_pb222_2020.c7_source_text: 'Antihypertensive treatment should be initiated expeditiously for acute-onset severe hypertension (systolic blood pressure of 160 mm Hg or more or diastolic blood pressure of 110 mm Hg or more, or both) that is confirmed as persistent (15 minutes or more). The available literature suggests that antihypertensive agents should be administered within 30-60 minutes.' Maternal stroke/eclampsia in minutes-to-hours.
acog_preeclampsia_pb222_2020.c8_source_text: Multiple explicit contraindications/cautions: ACE inhibitors and ARBs contraindicated in pregnancy; ergotamine avoided postpartum (severe HTN); magnesium toxicity thresholds (Table 2) requiring dose reduction in renal impairment; expectant management precluded by conditions in Box 4 (e.g. eclampsia, HELLP, abruption, non-reassuring fetal status); aspirin avoided as seizure prophylaxis.
acog_preeclampsia_pb222_2020._c9_note: Practice Bulletin uses Boxes 1-4 (risk factors, diagnostic criteria, severe features, conditions precluding expectant management) and Tables 1-3 (clinical risk factors, magnesium serum concentration, antihypertensive agents) but NO flowchart/algorithm figures in the 2020 PB 222.
acog_preeclampsia_pb222_2020.c10_source_text: Severe BP confirmed persistent '15 minutes or more'; 'antihypertensive agents should be administered within 30-60 minutes'; labetalol 20-80 mg every 10-30 min; hydralazine every 20-40 min; nifedipine repeat 20 min; delivery at '37 weeks of gestation or later' for any severity; magnesium continued 24 hours postpartum.
acog_preeclampsia_pb222_2020.c11_source_text: Acute severe BP control BEFORE delivery; magnesium sulfate seizure prophylaxis started BEFORE delivery in severe features and continued 24h postpartum; diagnosis (Box 2) BEFORE severity assessment (Box 3) BEFORE delivery timing decision.
acog_preeclampsia_pb222_2020.c12_source_text: Gestational HTN vs preeclampsia without severe features vs preeclampsia WITH severe features vs HELLP vs eclampsia → distinct management arms; gestational age thresholds 34 0/7 and 37 0/7 weeks gate expectant vs expedited delivery; 'In a patient who has preeclampsia with severe features before 34 weeks' gestation, expectant management can be considered'.

wms_heat_stroke_2024.guideline_name: Wilderness Medical Society Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Prevention and Treatment of Heat Illness: 2024 Update
wms_heat_stroke_2024._c1_note: WMS is a specialty society; listed in v2 rubric Tier-1 set (matches rubric inclusion of niche societies like WAO).
wms_heat_stroke_2024.c2_evidence_system: American College of Chest Physicians (ACCP) grading scheme (1A/1B/2A/2B by quality of evidence + benefit-risk balance)
wms_heat_stroke_2024._c2_note: [SUMMARY] 'These recommendations are graded based on the quality of supporting evidence and the balance between the benefits and risks or burdens for each modality' using the ACCP classification scheme. Society-adapted grading → score 1.
wms_heat_stroke_2024._c6_note: Environmental heat exposure is a climate-change-amplified cause; heat-related deaths rising globally but not in GBD Top-15; Lancet Commission flagged as emerging emergency.
wms_heat_stroke_2024.c7_source_text: [SUMMARY] Heat stroke (core temp >40°C + CNS dysfunction) causes mortality within 30 minutes if untreated; 'cool first, transport second' principle; target core temp 38.3-38.8°C as rapidly as possible.
wms_heat_stroke_2024.c8_source_text: [SUMMARY + search results] 'The WMS recommends against the use of dantrolene or antipyretic agents for the treatment of heat stroke (strong recommendation, moderate-quality evidence)'; 'Antipyretic agents such as aspirin, ibuprofen, and acetaminophen are not recommended in heat stroke because fever and heat stroke raise core temperature through different physiological mechanisms'; delayed transport before cooling discouraged; alcohol rubs not recommended.
wms_heat_stroke_2024._c9_note: [ABSTRACT-based] 2024 update includes classification flowchart for heat illness spectrum (heat edema → heat exhaustion → heat stroke). Conservative count 1; reviewer to confirm against full PDF.
wms_heat_stroke_2024.c10_source_text: [SUMMARY] Target core temp 38.3-38.8°C within 30 min of cooling initiation; cold water immersion until core temp <38.9°C; cooling rate 0.1-0.2°C/min achievable with ice-water immersion; hydration during exercise every 15-20 min.
wms_heat_stroke_2024.c11_source_text: [SUMMARY] 'Cool first, transport second' — cooling BEFORE transport for exertional heat stroke; airway/breathing/circulation BEFORE cooling if compromised; core temp measurement BEFORE cold-water immersion decision.
wms_heat_stroke_2024.c12_source_text: [SUMMARY] Exertional vs classic (non-exertional) heat stroke branches to different cooling modalities (CWI preferred for exertional; evaporative + ice packs for classic/elderly); heat exhaustion vs heat stroke gated by CNS dysfunction + core temp >40°C.

erc_hypothermia_2021.guideline_name: European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: Cardiac Arrest in Special Circumstances (Hypothermia chapter)
erc_hypothermia_2021._c2_note: [SUMMARY] 'based on the 2020 International Consensus on Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Science with Treatment Recommendations' — ILCOR CoSTR applies GRADE methodology; score 2.
erc_hypothermia_2021._c6_note: Accidental hypothermia not in GBD Top-15 but ERC 2021 covers full arrest-in-special-circumstances including drowning, avalanche, toxic exposure — arguably GBD Top-30.
erc_hypothermia_2021.c7_source_text: [PMC 2021 Update] HT IV (core temp typically <24°C) 'Unconscious AND no detectable vital signs'; '<30°C (young/healthy): Risk of hypothermia-induced cardiac arrest'; principle 'Not dead until warm' means minutes-to-hours window for ECLS rewarming.
erc_hypothermia_2021.c8_source_text: [PMC 2021 Update] 'Not dead until warm: Prolonged asystole, unwitnessed arrest, low temperature are NOT contraindications to rewarming'; avoid rough handling/movement in HT II-III (afterdrop risk); peripheral temperature measurements unreliable in hypothermia (do NOT use); rewarming rate <=5°C/h upper limit; pacing generally not indicated until core temp >30°C.
erc_hypothermia_2021._c9_note: ERC 2021 Special Circumstances includes multiple algorithm figures: (1) accidental hypothermia triage algorithm, (2) Swiss staging flowchart, (3) ECLS decision algorithm / HOPE score. Conservative count 3 for hypothermia section; full special-circumstances paper has ~10-15 figures across all topics.
erc_hypothermia_2021.c10_source_text: [PMC 2021 Update] Pulse check over 60 seconds before CPR decision; rewarming rates 'Active external rewarming... 0.5-4°C/h'; 'ECLS achieves approximately 4-10°C/h with target rate <=5°C/h'; intermittent CPR intervals in severe hypothermia (<20°C: up to 10 min without compressions permissible); transport to ECLS center if core temp <30°C + cardiac arrest or instability.
erc_hypothermia_2021.c11_source_text: [PMC 2021 Update] 'Oesophageal or epitympanic temperature should be measured' BEFORE triage decision; 60-second pulse check BEFORE starting CPR; HOPE score calculation BEFORE ECLS activation; rewarming BEFORE declaring death in arrest patients.
erc_hypothermia_2021.c12_source_text: [PMC 2021 Update] Swiss HT I-IV staging drives management branch; core temp thresholds 28/30/32°C each gate different interventions (pacing, defibrillation attempts, epinephrine); HOPE score favorable vs unfavorable → ECLS vs standard care; K+ level threshold (>12 mmol/L traditionally considered futile for ECLS rewarming in avalanche victims).
